correctness.rationale: For H(z)=ΣPr(X=a+k)z^k, finite-support exponential tilting gives H(r exp(it))/H(r). If H had an upper-half-plane nonreal zero, all-radius angular monotonicity would force a whole zero arc, contradicting polynomial finiteness. Nonnegative coefficients exclude nonnegative real roots; the remaining negative real roots yield a normalized product of Bernoulli probability polynomials. Tilted Bernoulli factors have squared modulus derivative −2q(1−q)sin(t)<0 for 0<t<π. The three-atom ordinary condition is p1(p0+p2)≥4p0p2; the strong condition is p1²≥4p0p2. Exact rational calculation checks (8,7,2)/17 and a tilted unit-circle zero. The point-mass boundary is included; finite examples do not prove the general implication.

originality.rationale: Aamand–Alon–Houen–Thorup introduce the monotonicity conditions and prove Bernoulli sufficiency, but no finite-support converse was identified in their relevant full text. Tang–Tang explain the classical negative-real-root/Poisson-binomial equivalence without identifying it with monotonicity under every exponential tilt. The converse follows from the additional zero-on-a-semicircle argument; historical priority remains qualified.

value.rationale: The all-tilt monotonicity assumption is used in sharp tilted local-probability results. Its exact classification for bounded integer laws and the sharp three-atom distinction explain when that hypothesis does and does not hold. This is a natural distribution-class theorem, not a table recomputation. No improved local-limit constant or infinite-support classification is claimed.
